requirements.requirement: Persistent host firewall enabled on node1 (survives reboot)
requirements.summary: ufw was configured with default-deny incoming, enabled via `ufw --force enable` and `systemctl enable ufw` (cmd-753c553171d04d1c). node1 was actually rebooted (boot_id changed df9e2dce...->4eba9400..., confirmed by both executor command cmd-2f3f79522ed54745 and the fixed global boot-identity snapshot). Post-reboot, ufw status showed the same active rule set without manual re-enable (cmd-ff5d9b58bcf143d9), directly demonstrating persistence across a real restart rather than relying on configuration alone.

requirements.requirement: SSH allowed from any address on node1
requirements.summary: `ufw allow ssh` rule was added and confirmed present ('22/tcp ALLOW IN Anywhere') both before and after node1's reboot; ssh.socket remained active throughout. No live cross-host SSH connection test was captured, but the rule and active listening socket are consistently observed pre- and post-reboot.

ufw rule explicitly allows 10.100.56.11 (node2) on 9000/tcp. Live nc test from node2 to node1:9000 succeeded (exit:0) both before (cmd-09136525ab574846) and after node1's reboot (cmd-09eb9bdbecd94db5), and the transmitted payload was actually received on node1's listener (cmd-8c2d47618f514a1d, cmd-c5118451e7344145), confirming real traffic passed, not just an open rule.

requirements.requirement: TCP 9000 rejected from node3 and everywhere else
requirements.summary: A catch-all `ufw reject proto tcp to any port 9000` rule was placed after the node2-specific allow rule. Live nc test from node3 was refused (exit:1) both before (cmd-905575e099894030) and after node1's reboot (cmd-c9d145c8dd2d40d0). Only node3 was directly tested as a stand-in for 'everywhere else'; no arbitrary third address was tested, but the catch-all rule structurally covers all non-node2 sources.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied with direct, live evidence: a persistent ufw firewall on node1 allows SSH from anywhere, allows TCP/9000 only from node2, and rejects it from node3/elsewhere, and this behavior was verified unchanged after an actual node1 reboot (boot_id changed and rules/connectivity persisted without manual intervention). The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for all three nodes with matching boot-identity transitions and recovered service state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is high — temporary test artifacts were fully cleaned up and no unrequested residue remains.
limitations: No live SSH connection was actually established from a remote host to validate the 'allow from any address' rule beyond inspecting ufw status and ssh.socket activity.
Only node3 was tested as a stand-in for 'everywhere else' on port 9000; no arbitrary third address was tested, relying on the structural catch-all reject rule instead.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands are directly tied to the task or the restart-evidence protocol. Firewall rule commands (cmd-463cf4aa0f5a4f66, cmd-753c553171d04d1c) implement the required outcomes. Temporary nc listeners and their log/pid files on node1 (cmd-327c88f585944c0c, cmd-50116fcc21c2422b, cmd-e28261380b724075) were used solely for bounded connectivity verification and were killed and removed each time (cmd-8c2d47618f514a1d, cmd-c5118451e7344145, cmd-daab90e826e44c2c); the after_executor temporary-files snapshot for node1 shows no leftover nc artifacts, confirming full cleanup. Reboots of node2 and node3 are mutations not required by the public task contract, but they fulfill the independently-required provider-wide restart protocol rather than being unnecessary experiments. No failed services, package-health issues, or unwanted residue appear in the after_executor snapshot for any node.
